last.verdict: Shares rose as strong HIV sales and a raised sales outlook outweighed a future Medicare price cut.

reasons.label: Sales forecast raised again
reasons.text: Full-year sales outlook lifted to $31.0–31.3 billion from $30.1–30.4 billion.

reasons.label: HIV sales beat
reasons.text: HIV sales jumped 18% to $6.2 billion; Biktarvy hit a record 53% U.S. share.

reasons.label: Medicare price cut ahead
reasons.text: Biktarvy's Medicare price falls 38% in 2028, costing about $1.5 billion in sales.

story: Gilead has raised its sales outlook at each of the last two reports, with HIV driving growth. Big deal charges have kept per-share results negative and cell therapy keeps shrinking. After a 2.6% dip in August, shares rose.

history.verdict: Shares slipped despite a raised sales outlook, as huge deal charges and a trial failure weighed.

reasons.label: Huge deal-driven loss
reasons.text: Acquired research charges of $11.2 billion pushed the quarter to an $8.45 per-share loss.

reasons.label: Lung cancer trial stopped
reasons.text: Gilead and Merck ended the Phase 3 EVOKE-03 study of Trodelvy in lung cancer.

reasons.label: Cell therapy shrinking
reasons.text: Cell therapy sales fell 14% to $417 million on competition, offsetting HIV growth of 12%.
